--- title: Versions and citation description: latest vs dated vs monthly releases, how to pin a version, and how to cite OmicIDX. --- OmicIDX publishes three kinds of versions. They hold the same tables in the same layout; they differ in how long they last and how you use them. [Releases](../releases.qmd) lists the ones available now. | Version | Where | Changes? | Kept | Use it by | |---|---|---|---|---| | `latest/` | `https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/` | rebuilt every night | always the newest | querying in place | | Dated | `https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` | never | 30 days | querying in place | | Monthly release | HuggingFace dataset [`seandavis/omicidx`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/seandavis/omicidx), git tag `YYYY-MM` | never | long term, with a DOI | downloading, then querying locally | `latest/` and the dated folders are served for querying in place: DuckDB `ATTACH`, `read_parquet`, omicidxr, and the [playground](../playground.qmd) all read them over HTTPS. The monthly releases are the long-term archive and the version to cite. Download one, then query it locally. ## Which one to use - **Exploring, or building something that should track NCBI:** use `latest/`. - **An analysis you'll rerun in the next few weeks:** pin a dated folder. - **A paper, a shared pipeline, or anything you'll cite:** download a monthly release. ## Pin a dated folder Replace `latest/` with a date: ```{.sql .no-shell} SELECT count(*) FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/v2026-10-20/sradb/study.parquet'); ``` To see which dates are available, open [Releases](../releases.qmd) or the [folder listing](https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/). Dated folders older than 30 days are deleted. Use a monthly release for anything longer. ::: callout-caution In dated folders published before late October 2026, `omicidx.duckdb` and `views.sql` point at `latest/`, not at their own folder. For those dates, pin with `read_parquet` on the dated URLs, as above. ::: ## Use a monthly release Once a month, one nightly build is copied to the HuggingFace dataset `seandavis/omicidx` and tagged with its month (e.g. `2026-10`). Files sit at the repository root in the same layout as R2 (`sra_runs.parquet`, `sradb/study.parquet`, …). Download the release with the [`hf` command-line tool](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli) (in `huggingface_hub`; `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf` runs it without installing), then query the local files: ```bash hf download seandavis/omicidx --repo-type dataset --revision 2026-10 \ --local-dir omicidx-2026-10 duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'omicidx-2026-10/sradb/study.parquet'" ``` `--include 'sradb/*'` downloads only some of the files. A [HuggingFace token](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens) (`hf auth login`) raises the download rate limits. In R, `omicidx_download("2026-10", "omicidx-2026-10.duckdb")` builds a local DuckDB database from a monthly release and checks its row counts (see [omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd#a-local-copy)). For `latest/` and dated folders, [`restore.sql`](duckdb-snapshot.qmd#work-offline) does the same from the command line. DuckDB can also read a release in place with `hf://` paths, where `@tag` pins the release: ```{.sql .no-shell} SELECT count(*) FROM 'hf://datasets/seandavis/omicidx@2026-10/sradb/study.parquet'; ``` That's fine for a quick look, but HuggingFace limits anonymous requests to 3000 per 5 minutes per IP address, and a query can make hundreds, so repeated queries soon fail with HTTP 429. Download for real work. ## Cite OmicIDX Each monthly release gets a DOI, minted on HuggingFace. Cite the DOI of the release you used, which you'll find on the dataset page for that tag. In your methods, also state the release tag (e.g. `2026-10`). If you used a dated folder instead, record its URL and the `transform_sha` and `lake_snapshot_id` from its `manifest.json`. The folder will be gone in 30 days, so a monthly release is the better thing to cite. ## The manifest Every version has a `manifest.json`: ```bash curl -s https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json ``` DuckDB reads it directly. The provenance fields of the current `latest/`: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT publish_date, dated_path, transform_sha, lake_snapshot_id FROM read_json('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json'); ```
Table: 1 records |publish_date |dated_path |transform_sha | lake_snapshot_id| |:------------|:------------|:----------------------------------------|----------------:| |2026-10-23 |v2026-10-23/ |2a999e937697b61bfdb3294de36582dd1cc5ab1f | 4239|
::: And the row count of each published table: ::: {.cell} ```{.sql .cell-code} SELECT t.schema, t."table", t.row_count FROM read_json('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json'), unnest(tables) AS u(t) ORDER BY t.schema, t."table"; ```
Table: 28 records |schema |table | row_count| |:---------|:-----------------------------|---------:| |geometadb |geo_supplemental_files | 7098064| |geometadb |gpl | 29060| |geometadb |gse | 298108| |geometadb |gse_gpl | 345076| |geometadb |gse_gsm | 10562000| |geometadb |gsm | 8774090| |main |bioprojects | 1130284| |main |biosamples | 60484224| |main |geo_platforms | 29060| |main |geo_samples | 8774090| |main |geo_series | 298108| |main |geo_series_with_rnaseq_counts | 27714| |main |pubmed_articles | 41275240| |main |sra_accessions | 162991962| |main |sra_experiments | 42655706| |main |sra_runs | 45553970| |main |sra_samples | 44670639| |main |sra_studies | 775372| |sradb |experiment | 42655706| |sradb |human_runs | 8540117| |sradb |mouse_runs | 4415567| |sradb |rnaseq_runs | 9054381| |sradb |run | 45699354| |sradb |run_with_study | 45699354| |sradb |sample | 44670639| |sradb |sra | 45699354| |sradb |study | 775372| |sradb |wgs_runs | 9601400|
::: - `transform_sha` is the commit of the [pipeline code](https://github.com/seandavi/omicidx) that built the tables. - `lake_snapshot_id` is the snapshot of the internal lake the tables were exported from. - `tables` gives the row count of each published table. `raw_partition_counts` records how many upstream partitions each source had.
